 One Acre Fund reveals how much each farmer earns per hectare
 November 8, 2026 
 Aideloje Ojo 
 Agriculture 
 0 
 Spread the word 
 An average One Acre Fund Nigeria farmer earn N300,000 per hectare more than other farmers in the country as a result of the acquired technical farming knowledge and high quality seeds provided by the organisation.
 The Credit lead of One Acre Fund Nigeria, Alhaji Yusuf Kasala, stated this at the weekend while speaking with Journalists in Fisa village, Bosso local government area of Niger state.
 Kasala also commended farmers in Niger state for attaining over 95% in the refund of the interest free credit financing they accessed from the One Acre Fund, explaining that the credit facility covered provision of agriculture inputs including fertiliser, improved seeds and cash.
 He said, “We have discussed this severally, for example one of the major impact that we have seen is that an average One Acre Fund farmer earns far more than an average farmer in Nigeria, as high as more than N300,000 per hectare.”
 He explained that the number of beneficiaries in Niger state have increased from initial 150 in 2018 to over 40,000 farmers in 2026, which he said, indicates high level of acceptance and success of One Acre Fund in the state, adding that, “this is why we held the 2026 Farmers Mega Harvest Day celebration in the state to celebrate One Acre Fund farmers”.
 According to him, “Our farmers in Niger state are excellent in the repayment of input credit facilities given to them by One Acre Fund and this is the reason for the priority attention we are giving to our farmers in the state. We have arrangement for refund of the credit facilities in instalment which makes it possible for farmers to be comfortable in the repayment process. I can tell you that over 95 percent of the farmers are repaying the credit facility and this has encouraged us to expand our activities in the state to other local governments from Bosso, Paikoro where we started in 2018”.
 Kasala explained that the organisation has put in a robust measure to ensure farmers don’t default in repayment of the credit facility, adding that, “we have conditional pardon to cushion the effect of the group liability rule where someone or more defaulted. Other members of the group are now allowed to continue while only the defaulters are dropped”.
 In a remark, the traditional ruler of Bosso, Alhaji Mohammed Dada, commended the One Acre Fund for the positive changes now enjoyed by his subjects in farming communities.
 He said the living standards of the farmers in his kingdom have been tremendously transformed with bumper harvest while appealing to the management of One Acre Fund to relax some stringent rules on collective punishment on groups with defaulter explaining that only those who defaults should face punishment.
